reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address thermal transport, phonon scattering, or electronic conductivity. E1 discusses elastic/plastic deformation and phase stability, while E2 reports oxygen contamination during powder metallurgy and its effect on phase formation and embrittlement, not on thermal conductivity. The key premises about scattering mechanisms, conductivity reduction, and temperature-dependent behavior are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Oxygen impurities in HfNbTaTiZr act as additional phonon scattering centers.
Oxygen-induced phonon scattering reduces lattice thermal conductivity by ~30% above 300 K.
Below 200 K, phonon freeze-out minimizes the effect of oxygen on lattice conductivity.
Electronic conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr exhibits a nearly linear temperature dependence governed by chemical disorder.
Ab initio simulations can capture oxygen impurity scattering and local chemical disorder effects on transport.
